say: March, twenty forty nine. The first war in space just broke out. And it started over ice.
Fourteen nations now live on the Moon. The Artemis Coalition: America, Britain, France, Italy, Israel, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand.
Against them, the Lunar Pact: China, Russia, North Korea and Iran. India and Brazil stay neutral.
Everyone wants the same thing: frozen water, hidden in the dark craters of the south pole. Water means air, fuel, and power.
Day one. At Shackleton crater, an American mining rover and a Chinese one claim the same ice field. Nobody backs down.
Day three. The Pact strikes first. Chinese and Russian armored rovers pour over from the far side, and seize Shoemaker and Haworth craters.
On the Moon, there's no air. No smoke, no sound. And a shell flies six times farther than on Earth.
The Coalition digs in on Shackleton's rim. British and French engineers turn ice mines into fortresses.
Back on Earth, everything spirals. Satellites go dark. Markets crash. Warships face off in the Pacific.
Day nineteen. Pact artillery hits India's base at Shiv Shakti point. India joins the Coalition.
Day twenty four. A surprise. North Korean landers touch down in Mare Crisium. Australia, New Zealand and South Korea race north to stop them.
The battle of Crisium lasts nine days. The landers run out of oxygen before they run out of ammo.
Day thirty one. On the far side, Russia switches on a mass driver: a magnetic railway that flings rocks into orbit. Every Coalition satellite is now a target.
Day thirty five. British and Israeli commandos cross the far side in total darkness, and blow the mass driver apart.
Day forty. The Coalition counterattacks. American and Israeli brigades push south from Tranquility Base, and retake Haworth crater.
Iran sends supply ships around the far side. But every convoy takes three days. The Pact is running dry.
Day sixty two. The front freezes along the rim of the south pole. Neither side can move. Neither side can win.
Day seventy. The Pact throws everything at de Gerlache crater. The offensive collapses in six hours.
Almost twenty thousand troops committed. Over four thousand casualties. For a few billion tons of ice.
Then the Sun steps in. A massive solar storm floods the Moon with radiation. Both armies hide underground for a week. Nobody fights. And that's when the phones start ringing.
Then Brazil invites everyone to Rio. Forty days of talks.
The Treaty of Tranquility. The poles become a shared zone. The ice belongs to everyone. And weapons are banned from the Moon. Forever.
The first war in space ended exactly where it started. Over water.
Which side would you have joined? Tell me in the comments.
